ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 93 of 2021 amending Law No. 78 of 2010 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing; Ministerial Decree No. 123 of 2021 establishing the Beneficial Ownership Register at the Ministry of Justice

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against Egyptian PEP lists, UN sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, EU sanctions, and domestic adverse media checks per AML/CFT guidelines

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Commercial Registry Portal (CRB) under the Ministry of Justice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official registration documents must be in Arabic; Latin-script foreign names permitted but require Arabic translation and transliteration per commercial registry rules
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical to or closely resembling government ministries, public institutions, or existing registered companies without approval
Words implying public service, religious, or political connotations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File administrative appeal with the Minister of Trade and Industry within 15 days of rejection notice, providing supporting documentation and detailed justification

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices generally not accepted for standard LLCs; physical Egyptian address required, though registered agent services with legitimate business address may be utilized if compliant
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium risk of unannounced on-site inspections by commercial registry, tax authorities, or regulatory bodies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Egypt LLC formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO due diligence and AML screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for international due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Executive Regulations), Articles 1-34 on Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 5-24 establishing GAFI one-stop-shop registration; Law No. 67 of 2016 (Value Added Tax) for post-formation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry (Tasgel Al-Sherkat) and Commercial Registration Office, operating jointly under the one-stop-shop system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Meethaq Al-Ta'sis) executed as a notarized public deed, together with the Capital Subscription Schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Companies Law No. 159/1981 as amended; founding members determine adequate capital based on notified scope; no escrow account mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolution No. 1-2025 adopted by the Board of Members of [EG LLC] at its inaugural session: (1) ratify the Articles of Association as registered with GAFI; (2) approve the allotment and issuance of fully paid shares to founding members per the capital subscription schedule; (3) adopt the notified Registered Office address at [address], Egypt, as the statutory headquarters; (4) appoint [Name] as General Manager with full day-to-day authority; (5) appoint [Name] as Compliance Secretary; and (6) authorize the General Manager to open banking accounts, retain external auditors, and effect all registrations with the Egyptian Tax Authority, social insurance, and the Commercial Registry. Unanimously approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Portal (Invest in Egypt e-Platform) or GAFI One-Stop Shop, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an investor account on the GAFI digital platform; submit three proposed trade names in Arabic (plus optional English transliteration); the automated screening checks the Commercial Registry database for identical or confusingly similar names; reserve the approved name with payment of the statutory fee. Name reservation is valid for one year.
required_dossiers: Valid national ID or passport copies of all founding members
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a written appeal with GAFI Legal Affairs Department or submit a revised alternative name within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Tasjel) in coordination with the GAFI e-signature attestation system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in Arabic using the standard GAFI template; affix the legally required fiscal stamps; each founding member must sign before a licensed Notary Public; the notary verifies legal capacity and compliance with Law 159/1981; upload the executed deed and specimen signatures to the GAFI portal for authentication.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Passport or national ID copies of all members
Capital subscription schedule with contribution method
Notarized power of attorney if signing by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the deed due to insufficient stamps or defective wording, re-execute the corrected deed with proper fiscal stamps and circulate for re-signature within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Shabaka Wahida) - GAFI Main Branch or Egyptian Digital Companies Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Association with the GAFI one-stop shop; GAFI verifies the deed against the Companies Law, collects stamp duty and administrative fees, and issues the Certificate of Establishment together with the company seal registration; legal personality commences on the date of issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query, respond within 15 days with corrected documentation; escalate unresolved delays to the GAFI Complaints Unit; amend and re-notarize the deed if substantive changes are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry, operated through the GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Registration application together with the Certificate of Establishment; the registry assigns the Commercial Registration Number (El Sijel El Togary); the entry is automatically linked to the Egyptian Tax Authority and the Central Bank of Egypt data systems.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease contract or title deed
Tax identification number or concurrent tax registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any discrepancy between the declared activities in the Articles and the Commercial Registry entries; file the amended registry page and pay the nominal penalty for irregularity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Central Registration Division and local tax office of jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit ETA Tax Registration Form No. 1 with incorporation documents; ETA issues the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and Tax Card; VAT registration is mandatory from full annual taxable supply exceeding EGP 500,000, with optional registration below the threshold; secure the tax card before opening bank accounts and invoicing clients.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA assigns an incorrect classification or refuses registration, file a written objection and request technical review by the registration committee within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) - Central Companies Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer using NOSI Forms 1 and 2; declare each employee and founding member working in the entity; NOSI assigns the employer social insurance number; the company must file monthly payroll declarations and remit combined statutory contributions against the insured salary subject to statutory caps.
required_dossiers: Particulars of founding members and employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI flags under-declared salaries, amend the declaration retroactively and negotiate an installment plan for any arrears through the NOSI collection department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI) Licensing Center and General Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - no industrial production license applicable to a non-manufacturing digital design office under ISIC 7410
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Office Operating Clearance (Rokhsat Tashghil) for service premises; no industrial manufacturing permit required for UI/UX design subscription activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'C' - Service and Software Establishment: exempt from an EIA Report under Law No. 4 of 1994 and its EIA Guidelines; a Letter of Environmental Exemption may be issued through the GAFI One-Stop Shop upon request.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 93/1962 for domestic wastewater discharge to municipal sewer lines; application of Law No. 202 of 2020 for separated office waste and e-waste disposal through licensed recyclers; no VOC or combustion emission sources for a digital design office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance (Eshhad Itfa) from the Civil Defense Authority covering alarm systems, extinguishers and evacuation signage per the Egyptian Fire Code; occupational safety inspection under Law No. 12 of 2003 by the Ministry of Manpower, including structural load verification and employee workstation compliance for the office lease premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), official unified tax and e-invoicing portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (eTax platform).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), the EG_LLC must file the unified tax registration application at the competent ETA tax office or via the eTax portal on www.eta.gov.eg. Submission requires: GAFI incorporation certificate, notarized memorandum of association / articles of incorporation, certificate of the legal address (office lease), passport copies of the managers and shareholders, power of attorney appointing an Egyptian tax representative, and proof of opening an Egyptian bank account. The ETA then issues the 9-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the tax card (bitaka dharibiya), and activates the taxpayer in the VAT, payroll, and e-invoicing registries.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not maintain a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification regime under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005; an LLC is mandatorily taxed as a resident corporation at entity level. No pass-through election is available. A foreign investor may elect to operate through a branch treated as a permanent establishment instead of an LLC, but the branch remains entity-level taxed. Egypt applies limited special-regime elections for free-zone enterprises (e.g., 5% of turnover or tax exemption subject to GAFI and ETA approval); none qualify as a US-style classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies (including export zero-rated supplies) in the preceding 12 months; mandatory registration for persons exceeding that threshold, with voluntary registration allowed for lower-turnover exporters to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt enforces a mandatory e-invoice and e-receipt regime introduced under Ministerial Decree No. 489 of 2020. VAT-registered taxpayers phased into the system must issue XML/JSON e-invoices and e-receipts through ETA-approved billing applications, transmit them to the ETA platform for real-time validation and clearance, integrate via the ETA REST APIs (contracting, signing and acceptance APIs), apply a qualified digital signature, and print or display a QR code on e-receipts. Issuance in electronic form is mandatory for all B2B and B2C documentation; rejected invoices do not produce a fiscal effect.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT zero-rating applies to (i) physical exports of goods leaving Egypt and evidenced by a stamped customs export declaration, and (ii) cross-border services supplied to a non-resident beneficiary for direct use and economic enjoyment outside Egypt, which includes UI/UX design subscription services delivered digitally provided the foreign customer is the sole beneficial recipient. The exporter must hold a valid VAT registration and tax card, produce the export contract and customer purchase orders, receive consideration in convertible foreign currency through an Egyptian licensed bank, and maintain full digital records of service delivery. If the service is partly used or enjoyed within Egypt, zero-rating may be proportionally denied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (final settled ACI/ACS export declaration certified by the Egyptian Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / international CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (Foreign Transactions Return Certificate - FTRC) issued by an authorized Egyptian bank confirming receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit zero-rating claims within the 5-year retrospective assessment period. If goods are not actually exported, payments are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory window, or the services are determined to be supplied or enjoyed in Egypt, the ETA will reverse the zero-rating, assess the 14% standard VAT on the gross consideration, charge default interest and late-payment monthly penalties from the original return due date, and impose administrative fines under Law No. 67 of 2016. Deliberate use of forged customs declarations or fictitious FTRCs, or aiding non-residents to simulate exports, constitutes criminal tax evasion referred to the Economic Court and attracts imprisonment, additional fines up to the tax evaded, and loss of all export incentive and refund rights. The clawback is joint and several against the taxpayer and its legal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Al-Bank al-Markazi al-Misri, acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) as the sole monetary, licensing and foreign-exchange regulatory authority of the Arab Republic of Egypt
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a liberalized interbank foreign-exchange framework. Following the March 2024 CBE decision to unify the EGP/USD market and remove exchange-rate restrictions, both current-account service receipts (including cross-border design subscription revenue) and capital-account remittances are, in principle, freely convertible through authorized banks. In practice, every outward flow requires a declared purpose, full AML documentation and available interbank liquidity, and profit remittance is conditional on an Egyptian Tax Authority clearance certificate confirming that corporate and withholding-tax obligations under Law No. 91 of 2005 have been settled. Inward equity is protected by the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 guarantees, which permit unrestricted transfer of investment proceeds subject to standard bank documentation. Treasury-prudent selection of banks with strong nostro liquidity (NBE, CIB, HSBC) mitigates any temporary interbank FX tightness.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For invisible exports, including UI/UX design subscription services, CBE regulations require that foreign-currency proceeds be received in an Egyptian authorized bank within 90 days from the date of service provision or contractual due date, extendable to a maximum of 180 days with documented justification. Under the post-March-2024 flexible exchange-rate regime, the historical 100% mandatory surrender at the official rate has been replaced by a full-repatriation framework: the entire export receipt must be credited to an EGP or foreign-currency account at an Egyptian authorized bank within the statutory window, with any conversion executed through CBE-authorized interbank channels. Unlawful offshore retention, delayed repatriation or under-declaration triggers CBE penalties, suspension of the exporter's banking facilities and transaction-level denial of future outward remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account plus Operational EGP and Foreign-Currency Account Structure
Operational EGP Account and Multi-Currency Corporate Account
Operational Account, FX Concentration Account and Trade/LC Facility
Cross-Border Optimized Multi-Currency Operational and Nostro-Clearing Account
Operational Account with Digital-First Onboarding Pathway

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury depository; Medium viability as an ancillary collection rail. Wise (the named target rail) holds e-money or banking licenses in the EU, UK, Singapore and other jurisdictions but does not hold a CBE payment-institution or banking license under Law No. 194/2020. It therefore cannot lawfully maintain an EG-LLC EGP-denominated treasury account, open a capital-escrow account, or act as a settlement agent for onshore Egyptian disbursements. Stripe Billing is similarly only a global payment gateway that aggregates subscription card transactions. The compliant architecture is a collection conduit: Wise and Stripe sweep USD/EUR receivables directly to the EG-LLC's designated foreign-currency account at a licensed Egyptian tier-1 bank via SWIFT MT103, with every settlement traceable to the underlying subscription contract and to the LLC's registered beneficiary name. Use of these rails without a local bank counterparty is not legally viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. CBE know-your-customer regulations require the original corporate documents, the board resolution appointing authorized signatories, specimen signatures and an in-person interview by at least one director or the appointed signatory at the bank's branch premises. Fully remote corporate account opening is generally not permitted for resident LLCs. Non-resident directors may delegate attendance through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of a resident manager or signatory; Egypt's accession to the Hague Apostille Convention, effective 14 July 2022, streamlines cross-border document legalization, provided the power of attorney expressly authorizes opening bank facilities, issuing FX undertakings and executing hedge documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident owned LLC with limited physical footprint, triggering 'ghost company' and economic-substance underwriting flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial registration certificate, GAFI investment or establishment certificate, tenancy or virtual-office contract with utility verification, VAT and tax cards, articles of association, directors' passports and national IDs, board resolution, specimen signatures and a factual statement of the subscription-design operating activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible digital-service exports with numerous low-value international clients aggregated through Stripe/Wise, raising unexplained-volume and trade-scope concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard subscription or licensing agreement, order-to-cash sample set, itemized invoices matching contracted design-subscription milestones, customer onboarding documentation capturing legal entity IDs or individual identification data, and a board-approved arm's-length pricing model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-currency receipts from online payment intermediaries that obscure the substantive end-payer, creating a money-remittance and payment-service-provider layering pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Wise settlement statements, merchant-ID credentials, beneficiary-alignment letters mapping the EMI and gateway rails to the Egyptian account, corresponding customer names and tax invoices, and a 12-month projected receivables schedule submitted to the bank's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, adverse-media or source-of-funds doubt regarding non-resident directors or shareholders funding the initial capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statements, home-jurisdiction bank references, audited financial statements of the shareholder, clean corporate-registry extracts, PEP declarations with evidence of legitimate business origin and a sworn undertaking in CBE-approved KYC format.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk-jurisdiction hits in the international client base or funding chain, given that Egyptian banks apply CBE, UN, EU, UK and OFAC screening to all wire traffic
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy, countries-of-operation list, subscription-client KYC pack, negative media review documentation and periodic transaction-monitoring reports prepared by the designated compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for shareholder capital injection: funds must be sent via SWIFT MT103 to the designated capital-escrow or operational account held at the selected authorized Egyptian bank, with the remitter being the sole corporate shareholder and the beneficiary identified as the EG-LLC capital-subscription account. The payment must carry a balance-of-payments purpose code corresponding to inward direct investment equity participation in the services sector, and the bank requires a debriefing file comprising notarized and apostilled shareholders' and board resolutions, the subscribed-capital schedule, the GAFI certificate or commercial registration reflecting the equity percentage and, where mandated, the CBE declaration-of-purpose form. Verification includes source-of-funds documentation and confirmation that the funds flow directly from the shareholder's corporate account rather than from an unlicensed third party, invoicing platform or cash-heavy jurisdiction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail hierarchy for the EG-LLC: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for routine operating expenses, contractor fees and software or infrastructure subscriptions, executed through the Egyptian bank's correspondent network with full FX availability checks and CBE purpose declarations; (2) SWIFT MT202 COV for priority correspondent-driven settlement where an intermediate beneficiary bank is interposed; (3) commercial documentary credits (UCP600) for any physical procurement or supplier arrangement requiring LC protection; and (4) domestic EGP disbursements for payroll, VAT, corporate tax and onshore vendors via the CBE-operated Egypt Interbank RTGS settlement system. All outward foreign-currency transfers require the underlying commercial contract, and dividend-type or profit-remittance flows additionally require the Egyptian Tax Authority clearance certificate. Where USD correspondent liquidity is constrained, treasury sequencing should prioritize statutory payroll and tax obligations ahead of discretionary distributions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable USD/EGP FX forward contracts with authorized Egyptian banks, tenor up to 12 months, supported by evidenced USD subscription receivables and denominated EGP payroll or operating liabilities.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with international counterparties only where an underlying cross-border exposure is fully documented and all EG-LLC proceeds are repatriated to the onshore interbank market; onshore banks generally prefer deliverable forwards for resident corporate hedgers.

Cross-currency swap (XCS) structures hedging EUR or GBP receivables against USD or EGP liability streams, including swaps on any foreign-currency shareholder loan, each subject to CBE-recognized hedging rationale, board-approved treasury policy and prudent valuation and collateral arrangements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the financial year-end (30 April for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 2% per month on unpaid tax; fixed late-filing penalty up to EGP 50,000; persistent non-compliance may trigger administrative enforcement and commercial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and General Assembly Approval Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: In compliance with Companies Law 159/1981, financial statements must be approved by the General Assembly within 6 months of the fiscal year-end; audited accounts must be filed with GAFI within 30 days of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EGP 1,000 for each month of delay in convening the General Assembly; repeated failure can subject the LLC to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registration Renewal / Continued Vigor Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 January following the close of the calendar year; must be aligned with the ancillary fee schedule published by GAFI.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a daily late fee of EGP 100; continued non-renewal suspends the company's legal capacity to contract and may lead to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Shareholding Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registrar / AML Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually upon commercial registration renewal and within 30 days of any change in ownership, share transfer, or pure beneficial ownership shift.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate UBO disclosure attracts administrative fines up to EGP 100,000 under Egypt AML Law No. 80/2002, with escalating sanctions for willful concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit for all Egyptian Limited Liability Companies regardless of revenue, total assets, or number of employees, as prescribed by Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and GAFI implementing regulations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are converged with IFRS standards as issued by the Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current Ultimate Beneficial Owner register. Any share transfer or ownership change must be recorded in the statutory register and submitted to GAFI within 30 days. An annual UBO confirmation certificate must accompany the commercial registration renewal, attesting to the accuracy of the shareholder and beneficial ownership records.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt does not grant a standard tax holiday for an LLC without industrial or export-zone status. The Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits a 50% reduction of taxable income for up to 7 years only for strategic zones registered with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI). For a standard ISIC 7410 UI/UX design subscription LLC, the effective tax rate will generally equal the statutory headline rate, subject to thin capitalization rules, depreciation elections and the availability of a 2x wage deduction for the employment of persons with disabilities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return – Form No. 8 (or the electronic corporate return within the ETA unified portal), filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing platform at eta.gov.eg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per fiscal year; no statutory quarterly filing, but companies subject to estimated tax must make three interim advance payments during the tax year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The form must be filed within four months after the end of the accounting period, together with audited financial statements and tax declaration annexes. A calendar-year LLC must file by April 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross subscription revenue from UI/UX design services, including all design-as-a-service billing before any VAT, stamp tax or other expense.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; the Egyptian resident LLC must report the revenue in Egyptian Pounds using the Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate for foreign-currency receipts settled through Stripe or Wise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, credit notes, chargebacks and discounts issued to customers during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident entry; the LLC must ensure that any reduction is supported by customer contracts and gateway settlement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of services, including freelance design compensation, outsourced developer fees, software subscriptions, stock imagery and data analytics tools directly consumed in delivering the UI/UX subscription.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Direct costs paid to a foreign related party are separately subject to transfer pricing documentation; a non-resident shareholder cannot claim this amount on the Egyptian return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit (Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computational line; no separate non-resident entry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General, administrative, operating, marketing and selling expenses, including rent, communication, professional fees, utilities and office costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses recharged to the Egyptian LLC from a foreign parent must be evidenced by written agreements, be at arm's length and satisfy Egyptian substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortisation in accordance with the Egyptian tax rules, using the prescribed declining balance rates for fixed assets and straight-line amortisation for intangibles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No entry by non-resident shareholder; the Egyptian LLC must keep a fixed-asset register and support the tax basis of each asset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax (Box 4 minus Box 5 minus Box 6), as derived from the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is a reconciliation point: non-resident shareholders should ensure intercompany balances match between the Egyptian entity and related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Addbacks for non-deductible expenses such as unlicensed donations, unreceipted entertainment, penalties, corporate income tax itself, provisions not yet written off, and interest on shareholder loans exceeding thin capitalization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees or royalty costs payable to a non-resident without source-record evidence are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset (Box 7 plus Box 8).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian jurisdiction taxes the worldwide income of an Egyptian resident LLC; a non-resident shareholder has no direct tax-filing obligation in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses utilised against current-year taxable income, limited to the residual balance of losses that arose within the previous five tax periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward belongs solely to the Egyptian LLC and cannot be transferred to the non-resident shareholder upon sale or asset transfer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss offset (Box 9 minus Box 10). If this is negative, the return shall declare zero and no refund is available for the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident entry; this figure forms the base for the corporate tax charge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax charge calculated at 22.5% of Box 11.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The withholding agent concept applies only at distribution stage; a shareholder cannot directly set off its home-country tax against Box 12.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim tax payments paid during the year, withholding credits, and any foreign tax credit attributable to Egyptian-source income of the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes borne by the non-resident shareholder on dividends are not creditable against this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due (Box 12 minus Box 13) or excess paid to be refunded or set off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian ETA must issue a final tax clearance certificate before the LLC distributes dividends to the foreign shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed refusal fine of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000 under Law 91 of 2005, plus a monthly delay surcharge of 0.5% on the unpaid tax, capped at 50% of the assessed tax. If the return is filed after a tax audit has started, an additional penalty of 5% per month or part thereof may be imposed. Failure to file for more than 90 days after the deadline permits the ETA to make a discretionary assessment and to suspend the taxpayer's tax-status card.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder seeking a reduced treaty withholding tax rate must provide the Egyptian paying entity with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, a completed Form WHT-TR (Treaty Relief Application), and written evidence of beneficial ownership showing that the income is not merely channeled through a nominee. The Egyptian LLC must submit these documents to the Egyptian Tax Authority together with a withholding certificate at least 30 days before the dividend payment date. The ETA will issue a stamped withholding clearance authorising the reduced rate. If clearance is not obtained before distribution, the LLC must withhold the statutory 10% and the non-resident may file a refund claim with the ETA within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by an Egyptian LLC to a non-resident for IP rights are subject to a 20% statutory withholding tax; interest paid on loans from a non-resident lender is subject to a 10% statutory withholding tax. Under Egypt's double tax treaties, the rates are commonly reduced to 5%–10% for interest and 10%–12.5% for royalties in arm's length transactions, subject to the TRC and beneficial-ownership certification above.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 15,000,000 in aggregate related-party transactions during the fiscal year triggers the mandatory preparation of a Local File. A Master File is required when the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 500,000,000. In all cases where related-party transactions exist, the Egyptian LLC must submit the TP declaration annex with the corporate income tax return and keep the full Local File, Master File and TP study available in the local jurisdiction for inspection by the ETA within 30 days of a formal request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted a dedicated UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute. However, Law 91 of 2005 and the associated GAAR provisions require that every transaction have a genuine commercial purpose and that pricing reflect the functions, assets and risks assumed by each party. For the ISIC 7410 UI/UX design subscription company, the ETA may recharacterise the whole entity as a tax-shell if it lacks an Egyptian office, senior design personnel, binding customer contracts, and independent decision-making. The LLC must maintain contemporaneous records of personnel, design project approvals, subscription pricing policies and bank accounts located in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Under-declaration of Digital Subscription Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or material under-invoicing of subscription revenues earned through Stripe_Billing or Wise, including diversion of customer payments to a foreign owner's personal account without recording in the Egyptian books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 and imprisonment of at least two years under Article 137 of Law 91 of 2005; the ETA will additionally assess the full tax due plus a 50% evasion penalty, and such administrative sanction may not be covered by insurance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs or who participates in the concealment may have the corporate veil pierced, becoming jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax, civil restitution of the diverted funds, travel ban, asset freezing and imprisonment if fraud or gross personal fault is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Profit Shifting through Transfer Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC pays inflated management fees, royalties or interest to a related offshore design subscription parent without substantial OPEX, personnel, contracts or economic substance; the foreign parent performs no demonstrable functions and assumes no commercial risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may adjust the taxable income to an arm's length result under Law 91 of 2005, imposing a 25% penalty on the additional tax assessed, together with a monthly 0.5% delayed-payment surcharge; the entity can be recharacterised as having a permanent establishment in Egypt and may lose the applicability of tax treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable to civil restitution for the TP adjustment and interest; if the arrangement is found to be a sham for laundering funds, directors may also be subject to criminal prosecution for fraudulent bankruptcy or tax evasion, inclusive of imprisonment and a court-imposed travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Non-Compliance in Subscription Collections
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report cash receipts above the statutory threshold received from unknown customers under design subscriptions; laundering proceeds through Wise or Stripe by mixing client funds with related-party invoices, or failing to verify the beneficial owner of corporate clients on the design contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, fines up to EGP 100,000 and imprisonment of up to five years, compulsory confiscation of the monies involved, freezing of bank accounts and deregistration of the LLC's commercial register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may personally face imprisonment, a travel ban and forfeiture of personal assets if they knowingly executed, facilitated or failed to report suspicious transactions; the corporate veil is pierced for intentional AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC distributes dividends to a foreign shareholder without withholding the required 10% amount and without obtaining a treaty relief clearance; alternatively, it withholds but fails to remit the collected WHT to the Egyptian Tax Authority within the statutory period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unpaid WHT is collected from the LLC together with a 2% monthly late-payment penalty and a fixed fine equal to 50% of the withheld amount; the ETA will also refuse to issue the tax clearance certificate, thereby blocking further dividend distributions and liquidation of the LLC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors of the LLC, as withholding and remitting officers, are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted WHT; the Egyptian financial courts may order direct attachment of personal bank accounts, a supervisory travel ban and, in egregious cases, custodial sentences.
